title: Prema Rawat Smashes 14-Ball Fifty, the Fastest in Women's T20 History
excerpt: The Uttarakhand allrounder came in during the 18th over, hit six fours and four sixes, and added two wickets for 12 runs in a record-breaking all-round display against Hyderabad.
body:
• India allrounder Prema Rawat scored an unbeaten 50 off 14 balls for Uttarakhand against Hyderabad — the fastest fifty in women's T20 cricket history.
  • Rawat walked in during the 18th over and hit six fours and four sixes, lifting Uttarakhand to 187 for 2; she then took 2 for 12 as Hyderabad were held to 98 for 8.
  • The previous record of 15 balls was shared by Marie Kelly, Fatima Sana and Laura Harris; Sana's 15-ball effort remains the fastest in women's T20 internationals.
  • Rawat, 24, made her India debut in June and was part of Royal Challengers Bengaluru's title-winning WPL squads in 2025 and 2026.

Prema Rawat walked to the crease in the 18th over of a Senior Women's T20 Trophy match in Pune on Monday and walked back with a world record. The India allrounder smashed an unbeaten 50 off 14 balls for Uttarakhand against Hyderabad at the MCA Stadium in Gahunje — the fastest half-century in women's T20 cricket, according to ESPNcricinfo.

"Prema Rawat walked to the crease in the 18th over of a Senior Women's T20 Trophy match in Pune on Monday and walked back with a world record."

Seventeen balls left, fifty runs scored

Uttarakhand were 129 for 2 when Rawat came in at No. 4 with only 17 balls remaining in the innings. She hit three consecutive boundaries off medium pacer Sakshi Rao, blasted 18 runs off an over from offspinner Vanka Pooja, and finished with 6, 4, 4, 6 off the last four balls bowled by Kunchala Niteesha to bring up the record. Her six fours and four sixes meant 48 of her 50 runs came in boundaries, at a strike rate of 357.14. At the other end, Raghvi Bist made an unbeaten 72 off 50 balls as Uttarakhand closed on 187 for 2.

Rawat then completed the all-round performance with the ball, removing opener G Kavyasree and N Kranthi Reddy to finish with 2 for 12 as Hyderabad managed only 98 for 8 in reply — a defeat by 89 runs.

The record she broke

The previous mark of 15 balls was shared by three players: England's Marie Kelly, who set it for Warwickshire in 2022; Pakistan captain Fatima Sana, who matched it for Pakistan in 2026; and Australia's Laura Harris, who reached fifty in 15 balls twice, for Otago in 2025 and Surrey in 2026. One distinction survives Rawat's innings: because her fifty came in a domestic match, Sana's 15-ball effort remains the fastest half-century in women's T20 internationals.

A leg-spinner rewriting the batting records

Rawat's primary trade makes the innings more remarkable. The 24-year-old is a leg-spinning allrounder who made her India debut in June this year and has taken seven wickets in seven T20 internationals, including 3 for 9 in an Asia Cup group match against Pakistan. She was part of Royal Challengers Bengaluru's title-winning seasons in the 2025 and 2026 Women's Premier League and has been retained by the franchise ahead of the 2027 season. A bowler who holds the world record for the fastest fifty in the women's game is, as calling cards go, difficult to ignore when India's selectors next sit down.
